explain.say: Imagine sailing for three years, not knowing how big the ocean is or if you will ever get home. In 1519, five ships left Spain to find a way west to the Spice Islands. Look at the chain: these are the steps of that voyage.

explain.say: They found a narrow, stormy sea path at the tip of South America, now called the Strait of Magellan. Then look: they crossed the huge Pacific for three months. Food ran out, and sailors even ate leather. How do you think they felt?

faq.q: Did Magellan sail all the way around the world?
faq.a: No. Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521. Juan Sebastián Elcano led the last ship, the Victoria, home to Spain in 1522, completing the first trip around the world.
asks: Who first sailed around the world?

faq.a: Lapulapu was a chief on the island of Mactan in the Philippines. In 1521 his warriors defeated Magellan's men, and he is remembered as a hero who resisted foreign rule.

faq.q: What is the Strait of Magellan?
faq.a: A narrow sea passage near the southern tip of South America that joins the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Magellan's ships took about 38 days to sail through it in 1520.
asks: How did Magellan reach the Pacific?

faq.q: Why did they want to reach the Spice Islands?
faq.a: Spices like cloves and nutmeg grew in the Moluccas, now in Indonesia, and were worth a fortune in Europe.

faq.q: Why was their diary one day behind?
faq.a: Sailing west, they kept chasing the Sun, so their days were a tiny bit longer. After going all the way around, they had seen one sunrise fewer than people at home.
asks: Why did they lose a day?

facts: The Magellan–Elcano expedition left Spain in 1519 with five ships and returned in 1522 with one ship, the Victoria, and 18 men.
Magellan was killed at the Battle of Mactan in the Philippines on 27 April 1521.
